answer: Place the compiled `.plug.js` next to the library page (e.g. `Library/yourname/yourthing.plug.js`) and list it under `files:` in the page's frontmatter. `Share: Page` does not upload it: it only publishes the library page, so you have to commit the `files` assets to the GitHub repository through other means.

--- Plugs/Development/Distribution and Testing.md ---
Distribution: ship your plug in a Library | Distribution: ship your plug in a Library
Plugs are distributed as part of a [[Library]] — the unit of distribution for all SilverBullet extensions. You don’t publish the `.plug.js` on its own. You publish a library page that carries it.

Follow this recipe in your own writable space. Publishing also requires a configured destination. The recipe mirrors [[Library/Development]]:

1. Create a [[Meta Page]] under `Library/yourname/Your Thing` with frontmatter that lists the plug file:

   ```yaml
   ---
   name: Library/yourname/Your Thing
   tags: meta/library
   files:
     - yourthing.plug.js
   ---
   This library adds …
   ```

2. Drop the compiled `yourthing.plug.js` next to the library page — e.g. `Library/yourname/yourthing.plug.js`. The `files:` list tells the library system to ship the plug along with the page when somebody installs it.
3. Publish the library page with the `Share: Page` command (GitHub file, Gist, etc.), which gives the page a public [[URI]].

--- Plugs/Development/Distribution and Testing.md ---
Distribution: ship your plug in a Library | Distribution: ship your plug in a Library
4. End users install it with `Library: Install` using that URI, or discover it through a [[Repository]].
5. Updates: push new versions of the library page via `Share: Page`.

See [[Library]], [[Library/Development]], [[Share]], [[Repository]], and [[Workbench/Libraries]] for the broader library system.

--- Plugs/Development/Distribution and Testing.md ---
Distribution: ship your plug in a Library | Testing & debugging > Live reload
Copying a `.plug.js` will be picked up by the sync engine fairly quickly. After this happens, a simple `Plugs: Reload` will (re)load the plug. No page refresh is required.

--- Library/Development.md ---
Decorate your library with frontmatter | Share the library
At this stage you can put your library file anywhere you like with a URL. However, for convenience, it’s good to use [[Share]] support for publishing.

For the purposes of this example, let’s use Github. Create a [[^Library/Std/Infrastructure/Github]] token and configure it as specified in the [[^Library/Std/Infrastructure/Github#Configuration|instructions]].

[[^Library/Std/Infrastructure/Github]] share support offers two options: Gists and Github repo files. Let’s use a Github repo.

[Create a new github repo](https://github.com/new), you can name it something like `silverbullet-libraries`.

In your own writable space, open the library page and run the `Share: Page` command, then select “Github file”. This will ask for a few things:
1. The repo name: enter your `user/repo` here
2. The branch name: you can keep this as `main`
3. The file name: while this defaults to using your full page, remove that and just name it e.g. `My Library.md`

--- Library/Development.md ---
Decorate your library with frontmatter | Share the library
4. A commit message

If all went well, an initial version of your page should now be uploaded to github, check your repo page.

You’ll notice that a few [[Share]] related frontmatter keys were set in your local copy. You can now make further changes to your library and run the `Share: Page` command again. After entering another commit message your page will be pushed again. This is how you publish new versions of your library for other people to use.

If you used `files` to include additional assets, you have to commit those to the repository through other means.

Your library is now ready to install, you can test this by running `Library: Install` in a fresh space. As URI use the value of what is generated under `share.uri` in your library’s frontmatter.
